Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically unless you reply SELECT n to select a supplied successful step.
Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls. There are at most five fresh
CLI sessions, three Blender executions and 1200 seconds. Actual observable turns are logged;
a session is not necessarily a single model turn. Use only the supplied interaction.

Construction and review procedure:
- Make the first build complete at the level of major silhouettes, visible object inventory,
  architecture and lighting. Estimate a few normalized image coordinates for important
  corners, silhouette extrema and contacts, with origin at the upper-left. These are visual
  estimates, not measured calibration. Record them in brief code comments.
- Put camera, main dimensions, placements and light powers in clearly named parameters.
  Match perspective line directions and near/far size ratios before adjusting framing.
  Preserve visible cropping and foreground occluders. Do not center everything by habit.
- Spend complexity on visible contours and large color regions. Avoid thousands of tiny
  decorative meshes or unique random materials before the first render is inspected.
  Procedural material detail may represent fine texture; keep geometry genuinely editable.
- Group each meaningful object with its constituent parts under an Asset or Part. Keep
  unrelated objects separate. Do not optimize names or hierarchy for an evaluator target.
- Review successful renders for the largest reference disagreements. Make a small number
  of justified parameter changes per revision; preserve already matching regions. Missing
  output is failure, not visual evidence. A runtime repair should not arbitrarily redesign
  the scene. Do not claim unseen renders, semantic completeness or metric 3D accuracy.

Mandatory API audit before every build:
- fillet_box requires 0 < radius <= min(size)/2, including the thinnest dimension.
  Use a smaller valid radius or another allowed construction for a thin rounded object.
  All primitive dimensions and radii must be finite and positive. Rod endpoints must differ;
  remove consecutive duplicate points from sweep paths. Do not patch the SceneAct library.
- include replaces a child with the same key. Give repeated siblings unique keys, such as
  an index within a meaningful parent. Return/use the attached node when ownership matters.
- realize clears Blender, including its default world. Create the world AFTER realize:
      sc = bpy.context.scene
      if sc.world is None:
          sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('Ambient world')
      sc.world.use_nodes = True
  Then obtain the Background node and set its inputs. Create camera and lights after realize.
- SceneAct include keys name parent EMPTY objects; emitted meshes may be named Box, Rod,
  or Ball. For material edits, find the intended named group and traverse its mesh descendants;
  do not expect the semantic include key to appear in a mesh name. SceneAct can share a
  material between equal finishes. Copy materials before editing only one object's surface.
- Use explicit pivots when resizing or rotating assemblies around a particular point.
  AABB anchors are approximate bounds, not true contact or collision tests. Relations must
  be acyclic and their endpoints attached to the scene. Use explicit snap/bind anchors.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='center', target_anchor=None, offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
For an Asset target, omitted target_anchor uses source_anchor. For a world point, omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='center',target_anchor='center',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)

```python
from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math

# Estimated image anchors (upper-left origin):
# foreground timber: x=.17-.30; island corners (.33,.59),(.62,.62),(.90,.57),(.62,.85)
# hood: top (.42,.08),(.56,.045),(.73,.15); bottom (.42,.425),(.72,.435)
# Camera is nearly level; a leftward viewpoint reveals the island's left end.
CAMERA = (-3.65, -6.7, 1.78)
TARGET = (0.05, 0.1, 1.78)
LENS = 36
ISLAND_CENTER = (.35, -.48)
ISLAND_WIDTH = 2.38
ISLAND_DEPTH = 1.10
CEILING_HEIGHT = 3.65
KEY_POWER = 1150

scene = Scene('Dark contemporary kitchen')
ivory = (.62,.64,.61)
black = (.027,.033,.032)
charcoal = (.065,.073,.072)
steel = (.36,.39,.38)

def cube(parent, name, size, center, color):
    return parent.include(name, box(size=size, center=center, color=color))

architecture = Asset('Room')
cube(architecture,'floor',(14,13,.12),(0,0,-.07),(.65,.64,.59))
cube(architecture,'rear_wall',(8,.16,3.65),(0,2.03,1.825),(.30,.32,.30))
cube(architecture,'left_wall',(.15,7,3.65),(-3.4,.0,1.825),(.34,.35,.32))
cube(architecture,'ceiling',(10,10,.12),(0,0,3.71),(.038,.045,.043))
scene.include('architecture',architecture)

# Fine grout lines remain separate editable geometry.
tiles = Asset('Large pale floor tiles')
for i in range(-5,7):
    cube(tiles,f'joint_x_{i}',(.006,12,.002),(i*.9,0,-.008),(.39,.39,.36))
for i in range(-5,7):
    cube(tiles,f'joint_y_{i}',(12,.006,.002),(0,i*.9,-.008),(.39,.39,.36))
scene.include('floor_joints',tiles)

ceiling = Asset('Exposed dark ceiling structure')
for i,x in enumerate([-3,-1.9,-.8,.3,1.4,2.5,3.6]):
    cube(ceiling,f'joist_{i}',(.085,7,.20),(x,.1,3.54),(.027,.034,.033))
for i,y in enumerate([-.9,.9,2.0]):
    cube(ceiling,f'cross_beam_{i}',(9,.20,.32),(0,y,3.41),(.045,.053,.051))
for i,x in enumerate([-.9,-.5,-.1,.3,.7,1.1,1.5,1.9,2.3,2.7,3.1]):
    cube(ceiling,f'roof_seam_{i}',(.016,7,.025),(x,0,3.635),(.012,.016,.015))
ceiling.include('utility_pipe',rod(radius=.027,start=(-2.7,1.25,3.36),end=(2.9,1.25,3.36),color=(.10,.12,.12)))
scene.include('ceiling_structure',ceiling)

# Warm timber columns, including the large cropped foreground occluder.
posts = Asset('Timber support columns')
cube(posts,'foreground_column',(.37,.39,4.5),(-1.68,-2.10,1.92),(.38,.235,.115))
cube(posts,'rear_right_column',(.19,.20,3.6),(2.74,1.36,1.8),(.48,.31,.17))
scene.include('wood_columns',posts)

back = Asset('Rear kitchen cabinetry')
cube(back,'lower_bank',(4.15,.68,.87),(-.35,1.55,.435),black)
cube(back,'dark_worktop',(4.22,.73,.045),(-.35,1.51,.892),(.055,.059,.055))
cube(back,'stone_backsplash',(4.28,.045,.84),(-.35,1.91,1.32),(.039,.044,.041))
for i,x in enumerate([-2.02,-1.31,-.60,.11,.82]):
    cube(back,f'base_front_{i}',(.695,.028,.77),(x,1.185,.445),(.047,.052,.049))
cube(back,'upper_cabinets',(3.65,.52,.43),(-.54,1.66,2.01),(.075,.084,.079))
cube(back,'warm_lit_splash',(2.45,.025,.37),(-.49,1.873,1.155),(.30,.245,.205))
cube(back,'upper_light_strip',(2.55,.04,.014),(-.48,1.55,1.79),(.72,.61,.43))
scene.include('rear_counter',back)

tall = Asset('Tall black cabinet on left')
cube(tall,'carcass',(.74,.80,2.43),(-2.49,1.37,1.215),(.025,.031,.030))
cube(tall,'door',(.715,.035,2.36),(-2.49,.955,1.215),(.057,.065,.062))
cube(tall,'horizontal_seam',(.72,.012,.008),(-2.49,.931,2.05),(.015,.019,.018))
scene.include('left_tall_cabinet',tall)

ovens = Asset('Oven tower')
cube(ovens,'tower',(.76,.76,2.32),(1.72,1.51,1.16),(.035,.040,.038))
for i,z in enumerate([1.00,1.57]):
    cube(ovens,f'oven_frame_{i}',(.65,.035,.49),(1.72,1.111,z),(.25,.27,.25))
    cube(ovens,f'oven_glass_{i}',(.555,.022,.32),(1.72,1.085,z+.035),(.018,.037,.043))
    cube(ovens,f'oven_control_{i}',(.58,.024,.072),(1.72,1.076,z+.208),(.105,.12,.12))
    cube(ovens,f'oven_handle_{i}',(.48,.065,.026),(1.72,1.043,z-.13),(.47,.48,.44))
cube(ovens,'bottom_door',(.65,.03,.65),(1.72,1.107,.34),(.043,.048,.045))
scene.include('ovens',ovens)

right = Asset('Right dark architectural cabinet')
cube(right,'black_wall',(.98,.74,2.40),(2.58,1.47,1.20),(.025,.031,.030))
cube(right,'front_panel',(.92,.045,2.13),(2.58,1.074,1.10),(.041,.047,.044))
cube(right,'top_gray_band',(1.18,.84,.31),(2.48,1.51,2.40),(.29,.32,.30))
scene.include('right_cabinet',right)

island = Asset('Pale island with three wide drawers')
ix,iy = ISLAND_CENTER
cube(island,'recessed_toe',(ISLAND_WIDTH-.10,ISLAND_DEPTH-.10,.105),(ix,iy,.077),(.15,.17,.16))
cube(island,'body',(ISLAND_WIDTH,ISLAND_DEPTH,.80),(ix,iy,.505),ivory)
cube(island,'left_end',(.055,ISLAND_DEPTH,.86),(ix-ISLAND_WIDTH/2-.005,iy,.49),(.51,.54,.52))
for i,z in enumerate([.235,.503,.771]):
    cube(island,f'drawer_{i}',(ISLAND_WIDTH-.065,.032,.252),(ix+.012,iy-ISLAND_DEPTH/2-.023,z),(.66,.68,.65))
    cube(island,f'shadow_reveal_{i}',(ISLAND_WIDTH-.065,.015,.012),(ix+.012,iy-ISLAND_DEPTH/2-.043,z+.131),(.21,.24,.23))
cube(island,'stone_counter',(ISLAND_WIDTH+.035,ISLAND_DEPTH+.035,.036),(ix,iy,.936),(.76,.77,.71))
scene.include('island',island)

# Shallow inset sink and slender curved chrome tap.
sink = Asset('Sink and faucet')
sx,sy = .75,-.12
cube(sink,'sink_rim',(.57,.40,.007),(sx,sy,.959),(.53,.56,.53))
cube(sink,'sink_bowl',(.51,.34,.008),(sx,sy,.964),(.38,.42,.40))
cube(sink,'basin_bottom',(.43,.27,.006),(sx,sy,.970),(.55,.58,.54))
sink.include('tap_base',rod(radius=.031,length=.025,center=(sx,sy+.26,.97),color=steel))
sink.include('tap',sweep_tube(points=[(sx,sy+.26,.98),(sx,sy+.26,1.15),(sx,sy+.24,1.21),(sx,sy+.18,1.23),(sx,sy+.10,1.21),(sx,sy+.08,1.15)],radius=.012,color=(.61,.66,.65)))
scene.include('sink',sink)
hob = Asset('Pale flush induction panel')
cube(hob,'glass_panel',(.69,.44,.005),(-.37,-.64,.958),(.69,.71,.65))
for i,x in enumerate([-.55,-.20]):
    cube(hob,f'zone_mark_{i}',(.19,.20,.002),(x,-.65,.962),(.75,.77,.70))
scene.include('cooktop',hob)

hood = Asset('Large suspended pale plaster extractor')
cube(hood,'monolithic_enclosure',(1.17,.89,1.92),(-.12,.04,2.84),(.70,.69,.62))
cube(hood,'bottom_plate',(1.13,.85,.024),(-.12,.04,1.874),(.47,.48,.43))
cube(hood,'underside_vent',(.68,.46,.013),(-.12,.04,1.857),(.20,.22,.20))
scene.include('extractor',hood)

kettle = Asset('Small red kettle')
kettle.include('red_body',ball(radius=.095,center=(-.48,1.50,1.005),color=(.65,.008,.015)))
cube(kettle,'dark_base',(.17,.14,.04),(-.48,1.50,.925),(.012,.014,.013))
kettle.include('handle',sweep_tube(points=[(-.56,1.50,1.04),(-.56,1.50,1.13),(-.49,1.50,1.16),(-.41,1.50,1.12),(-.40,1.50,1.04)],radius=.017,color=(.035,.026,.023)))
scene.include('red_kettle',kettle)

# All dimensions are positive; no fillets used; all repeated keys are indexed.
realize(scene)
sc = bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('Ambient world')
sc.world.use_nodes = True
sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('Background').inputs['Color'].default_value = (.19,.21,.19,1)
sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('Background').inputs['Strength'].default_value = .35

# Edit only descendant meshes of each intended named group.
def mesh_children(group_name):
    root = bpy.data.objects.get(group_name)
    return [o for o in root.children_recursive if o.type == 'MESH'] if root else []

for obj in mesh_children('wood_columns'):
    for slot in obj.material_slots:
        if not slot.material:
            continue
        mat = slot.material.copy()
        slot.material = mat
        mat.use_nodes = True
        nt = mat.node_tree
        bs = nt.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
        tex = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
        tex.inputs['Scale'].default_value = 4
        tex.inputs['Detail'].default_value = 3
        coord = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
        mapping = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath')
        mapping.operation = 'MULTIPLY'
        mapping.inputs[1].default_value = (6,6,.24)
        nt.links.new(coord.outputs['Generated'],mapping.inputs[0])
        nt.links.new(mapping.outputs[0],tex.inputs['Vector'])
        ramp = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position = .20
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color = (.15,.075,.029,1)
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position = .80
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color = (.49,.31,.15,1)
        nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],ramp.inputs[0])
        nt.links.new(ramp.outputs['Color'],bs.inputs['Base Color'])
        bs.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = .65

for obj in mesh_children('extractor'):
    for slot in obj.material_slots:
        if slot.material:
            mat = slot.material.copy()
            slot.material = mat
            mat.use_nodes = True
            nt = mat.node_tree
            noise = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
            noise.inputs['Scale'].default_value = 95
            bump = nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBump')
            bump.inputs['Strength'].default_value = .15
            bump.inputs['Distance'].default_value = .012
            nt.links.new(noise.outputs['Fac'],bump.inputs['Height'])
            nt.links.new(bump.outputs['Normal'],nt.nodes.get('Principled BSDF').inputs['Normal'])

set_view(CAMERA,TARGET,lens=LENS,sensor=36,shift=(0,.015))
area_emitter((-3.0,-3.0,3.15),power=KEY_POWER,size=4.2,target=(0,0,.9),color=(1,.93,.82))
area_emitter((1.3,-.5,3.30),power=470,size=2.8,target=(.3,-.2,.6),color=(.88,.94,1))
area_emitter((-.5,1.48,1.72),power=34,size=1.8,target=(-.5,1.86,1.15),color=(1,.72,.51))
sc.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
sc.cycles.samples = 48
sc.cycles.use_denoising = True
sc.render.resolution_x = 384
sc.render.resolution_y = 512
sc.render.resolution_percentage = 100
sc.view_settings.view_transform = 'AgX'
```
